'''Gudrun Pflüger''' (18 August 1972 – 17 August 2023) was an Austrian [[mountain runner]] four-time winner of the [[World Mountain Running Championships]] (1992, 1994, 1995, 1996).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wmra.ch/index.php/results/world-trophy-championships|title=World Trophy (1991-2008)/World Championships (2009 on)|publisher=wmra.ch|accessdate=20 October 2017}}</ref>

==Biography==
After retiring from the World Cup in Mountain running and xc skiing, she moved to Chelsea Quebec and later travelled in [[British Columbia]], [[Canada]], engaging in the study and conservation of [[wolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.patmos.de/pdf/rights/fact_sheet/978-3-8436-0141-2.pdf|title=Gudrun Pflüger Wolf Spirit - My Story of Wolves and Wonder |publisher=patmos.de|accessdate=20 October 2017}}</ref> During one field trip, Pflüger was spotted by the wolves she was studying and lay prone in the grass in order to try and lure them closer.<ref>{{cite web |title=The world's hardest scientists |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/gallery/2010/nov/04/hardest-scientists |website=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=24 September 2022 |date=12 November 2010}}</ref>

Pflüger died in [[Radstadt]] on 17 August 2023, one day shy of her 51st birthday.<ref>{{cite news |title=Eine mahnende Stimme ist verstummt: Nachruf auf Gudrun Pflüger |url=https://www.sn.at/salzburg/chronik/eine-mahnende-stimme-ist-verstummt-nachruf-auf-gudrun-pflueger-144000214 |access-date=22 August 2023 |publisher=SN.at |date=21 August 2023}}</ref>
